specification.scope: NEW lossless row-local arrow factorization of weighted regularized normal operators for the two SAVED522 projected numeric matrices. Preparation only; no LP algorithm, budget, witness or candidate.

specification.partition: Candidate local variables are native rootxy/f/legs15 and COM3 per nonfixed state. Joint g/p/load/drop and all command auxiliaries plus epigraph/eta are separators. If any row touches candidate locals in multiple states, promote ALL candidate-local columns on that row to separators. This deterministic one-pass promotion cannot introduce a new multi-state local row. No variable or row is deleted.
specification.exact_structure: Every original stored nonzero is copied into exactly one of B=A[:,local] or C=A[:,separator]. Every row of B has support in at most one state block. Thus B.T*diag(d)*B is exactly block diagonal in real arithmetic for ANY diagonal d. Signs, tiny nonzero coefficients, all rows, bounds, objective and equalities remain unchanged.
specification.operator: For strictly positive finite diagonal d,w define K=diag(w)+A.T*diag(d)*A. With local first, G=diag(w_local)+B.T*diag(d)*B is block diagonal, V=B.T*diag(d)*C, T=diag(w_separator)+C.T*diag(d)*C. K is SPD since v.T*K*v=sum(w*v*v)+sum(d*(A*v)^2)>0 for v!=0. Each G block is SPD.
specification.factorization: K=[[I,0],[V.T*G^-1,I]]*diag(G,S)*[[I,G^-1*V],[0,I]], S=T-V.T*G^-1*V. This identity is an exact-real algebraic theorem; a rounded Cholesky solve is not an exact inverse. S is SPD by the minimization identity y.T*S*y=min_x (x,y).T*K*(x,y).
specification.sparse_action: S*y=w_separator*y+C.T*(d*(C*y-B*solve(G,B.T*(d*(C*y))))). Never form K, V, T, S or a dense separator Schur matrix. Store only B,C and small local Cholesky blocks. RHS condenses to b_separator-C.T*(d*(B*solve(G,b_local))); recovery is solve(G,b_local-B.T*(d*(C*y))).
specification.numerical_example: ONE NEW operator-action/RHS example per saved system. Deterministic algorithm-unused separator y and b. d_i=2^(-2*frexp(max(1,sum(abs(A_i)))) exponent), w=1. Cholesky factors are of NEW weighted Gram blocks, not old L/K/Q mechanics matrices. No LP or Schur equation is solved.
